summary.text: Chellie Pingree is the Democratic incumbent for Maine's 1st District, which she has represented since 2009. Before Congress she ran a farm and a knitwear business on North Haven, served in the Maine Senate (including as majority leader), and led Common Cause. She sits on the House Appropriations and Agriculture committees.

paragraphs.text: Born April 2, 1955, in Minneapolis, Minnesota, the youngest of four children; moved to Maine as a teenager.
Attended the University of Southern Maine and earned a B.A. from the College of the Atlantic in 1979.

Moved to North Haven, Maine, where she and her husband ran a small farm, and in 1981 she started North Island Yarn (later North Island Designs), a knitting-kit business she sold in 1993; she also served on the school board and as town tax assessor.

Member of the Maine Senate from 1992 to 2000, representing Knox County; elected Senate majority leader by her peers in 1996. She sponsored the MaineRx prescription drug pricing bill in her last session.
Ran unsuccessfully against U.S. Sen. Susan Collins in 2002.
Served as national president and CEO of Common Cause from 2003 to 2007.

Elected to the U.S. House in 2008, the first woman elected to Congress from Maine's 1st District. She previously served on the Rules and Armed Services committees and currently sits on the Appropriations and Agriculture committees.

Received a 2017 James Beard Leadership Award for work on food system reform; her office says provisions of her agriculture legislation were included in the 2014 and 2018 Farm Bills. Co-owns Nebo Lodge, a bed and breakfast and restaurant on North Haven, started in 2006.
